sanskrit: vipattiṣv avyatho dakṣo nityam utthānavān naraḥ apramatto vinītātmā nityaṃ bhadrāṇi paśyati
english: The man who is unshaken in adversity, ever capable and diligent, vigilant and self-controlled — he always beholds good fortune.

sanskrit: antarvedyāṃ dadad vittaṃ kāmān anubhavan priyān krīḍan strībhir nirātaṅkaḥ praśāmya bharatarṣabha
english: Give wealth in charitable rites, enjoy desired pleasures, sport with women free from fear — be at peace, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca jānan vai mohayasi māṃ nāvi naur iva saṃyatā svārthe kiṃ nāvadhānaṃ te utāho dveṣṭi māṃ bhavān
english: Duryodhana said: Though you know, you confuse me like a boat tethered to a ship. Why are you inattentive to your own interest — or do you perhaps hate me?

sanskrit: na santīme dhārtarāṣṭrā yeṣāṃ tvam anuśāsitā bhaviṣyam artham ākhyāsi sadā tvaṃ kṛtyam ātmanaḥ
english: These sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra are not yours to instruct — you always speak of what will happen and what serves your own purpose.

sanskrit: parapraṇeyo 'graṇīr hi yaś ca mārgāt pramuhyati panthānam anugaccheyuḥ kathaṃ tasya padānugāḥ
english: One who is led by another and who strays from the path while being called a leader — how could those following in his footsteps keep to the right road?

sanskrit: rājan parigataprajño vṛddhasevī jitendriyaḥ pratipannān svakāryeṣu saṃmohayasi no bhṛśam
english: O king, though you are wise, a servant of elders, and master of your senses, you greatly confuse us who are engaged in our own affairs.

sanskrit: lokavṛttād rājavṛttam anyad āha bṛhaspatiḥ tasmād rājñā prayatnena svārthaś cintyaḥ sadaiva hi
english: Bṛhaspati has said that the conduct of a king differs from the conduct of common people; therefore a king must always strive to think of his own interest.

sanskrit: kṣatriyasya mahārāja jaye vṛttiḥ samāhitā sa vai dharmo 'stv adharmo vā svavṛttau bharatarṣabha
english: O great king, the livelihood of a Kṣatriya is concentrated in victory — whether it be dharma or adharma, such is his proper conduct, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: prakālayed diśaḥ sarvāḥ pratodeneva sārathiḥ pratyamitraśriyaṃ dīptāṃ bubhūṣur bharatarṣabha
english: Desiring the blazing wealth of his enemies, a king should illuminate all directions like a charioteer with a whip, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: pracchanno vā prakāśo vā yo yogo ripubāndhanaḥ tad vai śastraṃ śastravidāṃ na śastraṃ chedanaṃ smṛtam
english: Whatever stratagem binds the enemy, whether concealed or open — that is the true weapon of those who know weapons; a mere blade is not called a weapon.

sanskrit: asaṃtoṣaḥ śriyo mūlaṃ tasmāt taṃ kāmayāmy aham samucchraye yo yatate sa rājan paramo nayī
english: Discontent is the root of prosperity; for that reason I desire it. He who strives for advancement, O king, is the supreme statesman.

sanskrit: mamatvaṃ hi na kartavyam aiśvarye vā dhane 'pi vā pūrvāvāptaṃ haranty anye rājadharmaṃ hi taṃ viduḥ
english: One should not feel attachment to sovereignty or wealth; others take away what was formerly acquired — this, they say, is the law of kings.

sanskrit: adrohe samayaṃ kṛtvā ciccheda namuceḥ śiraḥ śakraḥ sā hi matā tasya ripau vṛttiḥ sanātanī
english: Indra made a pact of non-hostility and then severed the head of Namuci — that, it is held, is his eternal policy toward enemies.

sanskrit: dvāv etau grasate bhūmiḥ sarpo bilaśayān iva rājānaṃ cāviroddhāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cāpravāsinam
english: The earth swallows these two as a serpent swallows creatures in its burrow: the king who does not fight back, and the Brahmin who does not travel abroad.

sanskrit: nāsti vai jātitaḥ śatruḥ puruṣasya viśāṃ pate yena sādhāraṇī vṛttiḥ sa śatrur netaro janaḥ
english: O lord of the people, there is truly no enemy by birth; he with whom one shares a common livelihood — that person is the enemy, and no other.

sanskrit: śatrupakṣaṃ samṛdhyantaṃ yo mohāt samupekṣate vyādhir āpyāyita iva tasya mūlaṃ chinatti saḥ
english: He who out of delusion neglects a growing enemy faction — like a disease left to flourish — it will cut at his very root.

sanskrit: alpo 'pi hy arir atyantaṃ vardhamānaparākramaḥ valmīko mūlaja iva grasate vṛkṣam antikāt
english: Even a small enemy with ever-growing might devours the nearby tree from the root, like a termite mound that springs from the base.

sanskrit: ājamīḍha ripor lakṣmīr mā te rociṣṭa bhārata eṣa bhāraḥ sattvavatāṃ nayaḥ śirasi dhiṣṭhitaḥ
english: O Ajamidha, O Bhārata, may the fortune of your enemy not please you — this is the burden of statecraft borne on the heads of the strong-minded.

sanskrit: janmavṛddhim ivārthānāṃ yo vṛddhim abhikāṅkṣate edhate jñātiṣu sa vai sadyovṛddhir hi vikramaḥ
english: He who desires increase of wealth as one desires growth from birth — he flourishes among his kinsmen; for valor is indeed swift increase.

sanskrit: nāprāpya pāṇḍavaiśvaryaṃ saṃśayo me bhaviṣyati avāpsye vā śriyaṃ tāṃ hi śeṣye vā nihato yudhi
english: Without obtaining the sovereignty of the Pāṇḍavas I shall have no peace of mind; I shall either win that prosperity or lie slain in battle.

sanskrit: atādṛśasya kiṃ me 'dya jīvitena viśāṃ pate vardhante pāṇḍavā nityaṃ vayaṃ tu sthiravṛddhayaḥ
english: Of what use to me today is a life such as this, O lord of the people? The Pāṇḍavas grow constantly while our growth remains stagnant.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca yāṃ tvam etāṃ śriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍuputre yudhiṣṭhire tapyase tāṃ hariṣyāmi dyūtenāhūyatāṃ paraḥ
english: Śakuni said: That very prosperity which you see in Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Pāṇḍu, and which burns you — I shall win it by gambling; let the other side be summoned.

sanskrit: agatvā saṃśayam aham ayuddhvā ca camūmukhe akṣān kṣipann akṣataḥ san vidvān aviduṣo jaye
english: Without going into danger and without fighting at the head of armies, I, expert in dice, shall conquer those ignorant of the game by casting the dice unharmed.

sanskrit: glahān dhanūṃṣi me viddhi śarān akṣāṃś ca bhārata akṣāṇāṃ hṛdayaṃ me jyāṃ rathaṃ viddhi mamāstaram
english: Know my stakes as bows, O Bhārata, and know the dice as my arrows; the mastery of dice is my bowstring and gambling is my chariot-armor.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ayam utsahate rājañ śriyam āhartum akṣavit dyūtena pāṇḍuputrebhyas tat tubhyaṃ tāta rocatām
english: Duryodhana said: This expert in dice is confident of winning the wealth from the sons of Pāṇḍu by gambling, O king — let this be pleasing to you, father.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sthito 'smi śāsane bhrātur vidurasya mahātmanaḥ tena saṃgamya vetsyāmi kāryasyāsya viniścayam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: I abide by the counsel of my brother, the great-souled Vidura; conferring with him, I shall determine the right course of this matter.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca vihaniṣyati te buddhiṃ viduro muktasaṃśayaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ hite yukto na tathā mama kaurava
english: Duryodhana said: Vidura, free from doubt and devoted to the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas, will frustrate your intention — he is not so devoted to my welfare, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: nārabhet parasāmarthyāt puruṣaḥ kāryam ātmanaḥ matisāmyaṃ dvayor nāsti kāryeṣu kurunandana
english: A man should not undertake his affairs depending on another's ability — the minds of two do not accord in matters of action, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: bhayaṃ pariharan manda ātmānaṃ paripālayan varṣāsu klinnakaṭavat tiṣṭhann evāvasīdati
english: The fool who avoids danger and merely protects himself, standing like a wet mat in the rains, simply perishes.

sanskrit: na vyādhayo nāpi yamaḥ śreyaḥprāptiṃ pratīkṣate yāvad eva bhavet kalpas tāvac chreyaḥ samācaret
english: Neither diseases nor Yama waits for one to attain what is good; for as long as one is capable, one should pursue the good.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sarvathā putra balibhir vigrahaṃ te na rocaye vairaṃ vikāraṃ sṛjati tad vai śastram anāyasam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: In every way, my son, I do not approve of conflict with the mighty; enmity creates disorder — it is indeed an effortless weapon.

sanskrit: anartham arthaṃ manyase rājaputra; saṃgranthanaṃ kalahasyātighoram tad vai pravṛttaṃ tu yathā kathaṃ cid; vimokṣayec cāpy asisāyakāṃś ca
english: You regard what is harmful as beneficial, O prince — the binding of strife is exceedingly terrible; once set in motion by any means, it releases swords and arrows too.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca dyūte purāṇair vyavahāraḥ praṇītas; tatrātyayo nāsti na saṃprahāraḥ tad rocatāṃ śakuner vākyam adya; sabhāṃ kṣipraṃ tvam ihājñāpayasva
english: Duryodhana said: The ancients established gambling as a recognized practice — in it there is no excess and no clash of arms; let Śakuni's proposal be pleasing today — quickly command that a hall be built here.

sanskrit: svargadvāraṃ dīvyatāṃ no viśiṣṭaṃ; tadvartināṃ cāpi tathaiva yuktam bhaved evaṃ hy ātmanā tulyam eva; durodaraṃ pāṇḍavais tvaṃ kuruṣva
english: Gambling is for us an excellent gate to heaven, and it is likewise fitting for those who abide by it — thus make it equal on both sides; arrange a gambling match between us and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca vākyaṃ na me rocate yat tvayoktaṃ; yat te priyaṃ tat kriyatāṃ narendra paścāt tapsyase tad upākramya vākyaṃ; na hīdṛśaṃ bhāvi vaco hi dharmyam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: What you have said does not please me; yet let what is dear to you be done, O lord of men — having undertaken this course you will repent afterward, for such a word is not righteous.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭaṃ hy etad vidureṇaivam eva; sarvaṃ pūrvaṃ buddhividyānugena tad evaitad avaśasyābhyupaiti; mahad bhayaṃ kṣatriyabījaghāti
english: Vidura has already seen all this clearly with his wisdom and learning — yet this great fear, which destroys the seed of the Kṣatriyas, is coming upon us helplessly.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā dhṛtarāṣṭro manīṣī; daivaṃ matvā paramaṃ dustaraṃ ca śaśāsoccaiḥ puruṣān putravākye; sthito rājā daivasaṃmūḍhacetāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra, considering fate supreme and hard to overcome, loudly commanded his men in accordance with his son's words — the king stood firm, his mind bewildered by fate.

sanskrit: sahasrastambhāṃ hemavaiḍūryacitrāṃ; śatadvārāṃ toraṇasphāṭiśṛṅgām sabhām agryāṃ krośamātrāyatāṃ me; tad vistārām āśu kurvantu yuktāḥ
english: Let the workers quickly build for me a magnificent hall with a thousand pillars, decorated with gold and vaidurya gems, with a hundred doors, with spires of crystal over the arched gateways, a league in length and breadth accordingly.

sanskrit: śrutvā tasya tvaritā nirviśaṅkāḥ; prājñā dakṣās tāṃ tathā cakrur āśu sarvadravyāṇy upajahruḥ sabhāyāṃ; sahasraśaḥ śilpinaś cāpi yuktāḥ
english: Having heard this, the wise and skilled workers swiftly and without hesitation built it exactly as commanded; all manner of materials were brought to the hall, and thousands of craftsmen were engaged.

sanskrit: kālenālpenātha niṣṭhāṃ gatāṃ tāṃ; sabhāṃ ramyāṃ bahuratnāṃ vicitrām citrair haimair āsanair abhyupetām; ācakhyus te tasya rājñaḥ pratītāḥ
english: Then in a short time those workers reported joyfully to the king that the charming hall, filled with many gems, adorned with various designs, and furnished with golden seats of varied craftsmanship, had been completed.

sanskrit: tato vidvān viduraṃ mantrimukhyam; uvācedaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro narendraḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ rājaputraṃ hi gatvā; madvākyena kṣipram ihānayasva
english: Then the wise king Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke these words to Vidura, the foremost of ministers: Go to prince Yudhiṣṭhira and quickly bring him here in my name.

sanskrit: sabheyaṃ me bahuratnā vicitrā; śayyāsanair upapannā mahārhaiḥ sā dṛśyatāṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdham etya; suhṛddyūtaṃ vartatām atra ceti
english: Let this hall of mine, rich in gems and of varied design, furnished with most excellent couches and seats, be seen by him coming together with his brothers — and let a friendly gambling match take place here.

sanskrit: matam ājñāya putrasya dhṛtarāṣṭro narādhipaḥ matvā ca dustaraṃ daivam etad rājā cakāra ha
english: King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, knowing his son's intention and considering fate hard to overcome, did as commanded.

sanskrit: anyāyena tathoktas tu viduro viduṣāṃ varaḥ nābhyanandad vaco bhrātur vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: But Vidura, best of the wise, thus spoken to in an improper manner, did not welcome his brother's words, and spoke these words:

sanskrit: nābhinandāmi nṛpate praiṣam etaṃ; maivaṃ kṛthāḥ kulanāśād bibhemi putrair bhinnaiḥ kalahas te dhruvaṃ syād; etac chaṅke dyūtakṛte narendra
english: I do not welcome this errand, O king — do not do this; I fear the destruction of our clan. When sons are divided, strife for you would certainly follow — this is my apprehension arising from this gambling, O lord of men.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca neha kṣattaḥ kalahas tapsyate māṃ; na ced daivaṃ pratilomaṃ bhaviṣyat dhātrā tu diṣṭasya vaśe kiledaṃ; sarvaṃ jagac ceṣṭati na svatantram
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: No strife here shall distress me, O Kṣattā, if fate does not run contrary — for it is said that this entire world moves under the control of fate, in the power of what is destined, and is not independent.

sanskrit: tad adya vidura prāpya rājānaṃ mama śāsanāt kṣipram ānaya durdharṣaṃ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Therefore, Vidura, go today and by my command quickly bring back the invincible Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, the king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prāyād viduro 'śvair udārair; mahājavair balibhiḥ sādhudāntaiḥ balān niyukto dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rājñā; manīṣiṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ sakāśam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Vidura, compelled by force by King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, set out with noble horses — swift, strong, and well-trained — toward the abode of the wise Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: so 'bhipatya tadadhvānam āsādya nṛpateḥ puram praviveśa mahābuddhiḥ pūjyamāno dvijātibhiḥ
english: Having swiftly traversed that road and reached the city of the king, the great-minded Vidura entered, honored by the twice-born.

sanskrit: sa rājagṛham āsādya kuberabhavanopamam abhyagacchata dharmātmā dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Reaching the royal palace, which resembled the mansion of Kubera, that righteous-souled one approached Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma.

sanskrit: taṃ vai rājā satyadhṛtir mahātmā; ajātaśatrur viduraṃ yathāvat pūjāpūrvaṃ pratigṛhyājamīḍhas; tato 'pṛcchad dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ saputram
english: The king of firm truth, the great-souled Ajātaśatru, received Vidura with due honor as was proper, and then inquired after Dhṛtarāṣṭra and his sons.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vijñāyate te manaso na praharṣaḥ; kaccit kṣattaḥ kuśalenāgato 'si kaccit putrāḥ sthavirasyānulomā; vaśānugāś cāpi viśo 'pi kaccit
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: It is evident that your mind is not joyful — have you come in good health, O Kṣattā? Are the sons of the aged king compliant and obedient to him? And are the subjects also submissive?

sanskrit: vidura uvāca rājā mahātmā kuśalī saputra; āste vṛto jñātibhir indrakalpaiḥ prīto rājan putragaṇair vinītair; viśoka evātmaratir dṛḍhātmā
english: Vidura said: The great-souled king is well and is with his sons; he dwells surrounded by kinsmen like Indra, O king — pleased with his dutiful sons, free from sorrow, self-content, and firm of spirit.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu tvāṃ kururājo 'bhyuvāca; pūrvaṃ pṛṣṭvā kuśalaṃ cāvyayaṃ ca iyaṃ sabhā tvatsabhātulyarūpā; bhrātṝṇāṃ te paśya tām etya putra
english: But the king of the Kurus, after first asking after your well-being and imperishable health, has said this to you: This hall, which rivals your own assembly hall in splendor — come and see it with your brothers, my son.

sanskrit: samāgamya bhrātṛbhiḥ pārtha tasyāṃ; suhṛddyūtaṃ kriyatāṃ ramyatāṃ ca prīyāmahe bhavataḥ saṃgamena; samāgatāḥ kuravaś caiva sarve
english: Coming together with your brothers, O Pārtha, let a friendly gambling match take place in it for enjoyment — we rejoice in your company, and all the Kauravas too have assembled.

sanskrit: durodarā vihitā ye tu tatra; mahātmanā dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rājñā tān drakṣyase kitavān saṃniviṣṭān; ity āgato 'haṃ nṛpate taj juṣasva
english: The gamblers who have been arranged there by the great-souled King Dhṛtarāṣṭra — you shall see them seated; thus have I come, O king — be pleased with this.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dyūte kṣattaḥ kalaho vidyate naḥ; ko vai dyūtaṃ rocayed budhyamānaḥ kiṃ vā bhavān manyate yuktarūpaṃ; bhavadvākye sarva eva sthitāḥ sma
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: In gambling, O Kṣattā, there is strife for us — what thoughtful man would relish gambling? What do you yourself consider appropriate? We all abide by your word.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca jānāmy ahaṃ dyūtam anarthamūlaṃ; kṛtaś ca yatno 'sya mayā nivāraṇe rājā tu māṃ prāhiṇot tvatsakāśaṃ; śrutvā vidvañ śreya ihācarasva
english: Vidura said: I know that gambling is the root of disaster, and I made every effort to prevent it; yet the king has sent me to your presence — having heard this, O learned one, do here what is for the good.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ke tatrānye kitavā dīvyamānā; vinā rājño dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraiḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ vidura brūhi nas tān; yair dīvyāmaḥ śataśaḥ saṃnipatya
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who are the other gamblers there who will be playing, besides the sons of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra? I ask you, Vidura — tell us about them, the ones with whom we would gamble, assembled in their hundreds.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca gāndhārarājaḥ śakunir viśāṃ pate; rājātidevī kṛtahasto matākṣaḥ viviṃśatiś citrasenaś ca rājā; satyavrataḥ purumitro jayaś ca
english: Vidura said: Śakuni, king of Gāndhāra, O lord of the people — an expert gambler, skilled of hand and knowing the dice; Viviṃśati, king Citrasena, Satyavrata, Purumitra, and Jaya.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mahābhayāḥ kitavāḥ saṃniviṣṭā; māyopadhā devitāro 'tra santi dhātrā tu diṣṭasya vaśe kiledaṃ; nādevanaṃ kitavair adya tair me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Terrible and fearsome gamblers are assembled there — cheaters who play with deceit are present; yet it is said that this world is under the control of fate and what is destined — I shall not refuse to gamble with those gamesters today.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ rājño dhṛtarāṣṭrasya śāsanān; na gantum icchāmi kave durodaram iṣṭo hi putrasya pitā sadaiva; tad asmi kartā vidurāttha māṃ yathā
english: I do not wish to go for the gambling at King Dhṛtarāṣṭra's command, O wise one — yet the father is always dear to the son; so I shall do as you have told me, O Vidura.

sanskrit: na cākāmaḥ śakuninā devitāhaṃ; na cen māṃ dhṛṣṇur āhvayitā sabhāyām āhūto 'haṃ na nivarte kadā cit; tad āhitaṃ śāśvataṃ vai vrataṃ me
english: I do not willingly wish to gamble with Śakuni; but if the bold one challenges me in the assembly hall, when challenged I never turn back — that is the eternal vow I have taken.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā viduraṃ dharmarājaḥ; prāyātrikaṃ sarvam ājñāpya tūrṇam prāyāc chvobhūte sagaṇaḥ sānuyātraḥ; saha strībhir draupadīm ādikṛtvā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to Vidura, the king of dharma quickly gave all orders for the journey, and set out the next day with his retinue and attendants, together with the women headed by Draupadī.

sanskrit: daivaṃ prajñāṃ tu muṣṇāti tejaś cakṣur ivāpatat dhātuś ca vaśam anveti pāśair iva naraḥ sitaḥ
english: Fate steals away wisdom and splendor like a sudden blow to the eye; and a man goes under the control of the creator, bound as if by cords.

sanskrit: ity uktvā prayayau rājā saha kṣattrā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ amṛṣyamāṇas tat pārthaḥ samāhvānam ariṃdamaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, king Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Pṛthā, the subduer of foes, departed together with Kṣattā, unable to disregard that summons.

sanskrit: bāhlikena rathaṃ dattam āsthāya paravīrahā paricchanno yayau pārtho bhrātṛbhiḥ saha pāṇḍavaḥ
english: The son of Pṛthā, the Pāṇḍava, slayer of enemy heroes, mounted the chariot given by Bahlika and journeyed in disguise together with his brothers.

sanskrit: rājaśriyā dīpyamāno yayau brahmapuraḥsaraḥ dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa cāhūtaḥ kālasya samayena ca
english: Blazing with royal splendor, he went forth preceded by Brahmins, summoned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra and by the appointed hour of fate.

sanskrit: sa hāstinapuraṃ gatvā dhṛtarāṣṭragṛhaṃ yayau samiyāya ca dharmātmā dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Going to Hāstinapura, the righteous-souled Pāṇḍava proceeded to Dhṛtarāṣṭra's palace and met with Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tathā droṇena bhīṣmeṇa karṇena ca kṛpeṇa ca samiyāya yathānyāyaṃ drauṇinā ca vibhuḥ saha
english: The mighty one also met in due order with Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Karṇa, Kṛpa, and the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: sametya ca mahābāhuḥ somadattena caiva ha duryodhanena śalyena saubalena ca vīryavān
english: The mighty-armed and valiant one also met with Somadatta, Duryodhana, Śalya, and the son of Subala.

sanskrit: ye cānye tatra rājānaḥ pūrvam eva samāgatāḥ jayadrathena ca tathā kurubhiś cāpi sarvaśaḥ
english: And with the other kings who had gathered there before, as well as with Jayadratha, and with all the Kauravas in full.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvair mahābāhur bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ praviveśa gṛhaṃ rājño dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dhīmataḥ
english: Then the mighty-armed one, surrounded by all his brothers, entered the palace of the wise King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: dadarśa tatra gāndhārīṃ devīṃ patim anuvratām snuṣābhiḥ saṃvṛtāṃ śaśvat tārābhir iva rohiṇīm
english: There he saw the queen Gāndhārī, devoted to her husband, surrounded by her daughters-in-law, ever like Rohiṇī surrounded by stars.

sanskrit: abhivādya sa gāndhārīṃ tayā ca pratinanditaḥ dadarśa pitaraṃ vṛddhaṃ prajñācakṣuṣam īśvaram
english: Paying homage to Gāndhārī and welcomed by her in return, he then saw the aged father, the lord whose eyes were wisdom itself.

sanskrit: rājñā mūrdhany upāghrātās te ca kauravanandanāḥ catvāraḥ pāṇḍavā rājan bhīmasenapurogamāḥ
english: By the king were sniffed on their heads — those four Pāṇḍavas, O king, the joys of the Kauravas, led by Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tato harṣaḥ samabhavat kauravāṇāṃ viśāṃ pate tān dṛṣṭvā puruṣavyāghrān pāṇḍavān priyadarśanān
english: Then great joy arose among the Kauravas, O lord of the people, upon seeing those tiger-men among men, the Pāṇḍavas, beautiful to behold.

sanskrit: viviśus te 'bhyanujñātā ratnavanti gṛhāṇy atha dadṛśuś copayātās tān draupadīpramukhāḥ striyaḥ
english: Having received permission, they entered their gem-filled quarters; and the women headed by Draupadī came and saw them as they arrived.

sanskrit: yājñasenyāḥ parām ṛddhiṃ dṛṣṭvā prajvalitām iva snuṣās tā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya nātipramanaso 'bhavan
english: Seeing the supreme prosperity of Yājñasenī, blazing as it were, those daughters-in-law of Dhṛtarāṣṭra were not particularly pleased in their hearts.

sanskrit: tatas te puruṣavyāghrā gatvā strībhis tu saṃvidam kṛtvā vyāyāmapūrvāṇi kṛtyāni pratikarma ca
english: Then those tiger-men among men, having gone and conversed with the women, performed their exercises and other duties as was their custom.
